🔍 Top American generals warn Iran conflict stretching US forces to their limits
Six months into the Iran conflict, top US military commanders are sounding a dire warning: the armed forces are being driven to the breaking point—and they’re pushing back against Washington’s war machine.
According to a classified August 14 assessment obtained by The Washington Post, the heads of the Army, Navy, and Air Force—alongside four-star commanders overseeing Europe, Asia, and Latin America—delivered a blunt message to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: maintaining the current operational tempo in the Middle East is becoming "unsustainable."
🔴 The top military brass from the European, Pacific, and Southern Commands issued a formal disagreement with orders to continue providing ships, aircraft, and personnel to the Iran campaign, citing troop exhaustion and equipment wear
🔴 Admiral Daryl Caudle, the Chief of Naval Operations, painted the grimmest picture yet. He warned Hegseth that the Navy cannot keep up its current support level without a clear end date—especially with fewer than one in four destroyers currently ready to deploy.
🔴 The document also reveals that some Middle East–deployed forces—including key elements of the 82nd Airborne Division, the tip of the spear for any potential ground operation, along with Air Force and air-defense units—are now locked in through September, with others potentially staying until 2027
The strain on personnel tells only part of the story, the war is depleting America's arsenal. The Pentagon is facing dangerously low reserves of Patriot and THAAD interceptors, along with declining inventories of Tomahawk missiles, while restocking is expected to take years. Add to that the loss of roughly a quarter of the Reaper fleet and US forces now find themselves overstretched and exhausted, with no clear end to the conflict in sight as logistical and morale pressures mount.

events.text:
🔍 Inside the Polisario Front - The movement defying Morocco, Israel and US plots in Western Sahara
Western Sahara has been at the center of a decades-long geopolitical struggle, with Israel seeking to strengthen its foothold in Africa. The Polisario Front, much like the Palestinians in the Middle East, stands in the way of those ambitions.
Polisario Front and scars of Spanish colonialism
🔴 Founded on May 10, 1973, the Polisario Front (the Popular Front for the Liberation of Saguía el-Hamra y Río de Oro) represents the indigenous Sahrawi people and advocates for an independent Sahrawi state in Western Sahara
🔴 Spain withdrew from Western Sahara in 1975–76, handing control to Morocco and Mauritania – a move denounced by the International Court of Justice at the time. The Polisario Front proclaimed the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR) on February 27, 1976, and started its fight for independence
🔴 In 1991, the UN brokered a peace plan for Western Sahara by establishing a cease-fire, deploying peacekeepers, and calling for a self-determination referendum – but more than three decades later, the vote has yet to take place
🔴 Presently, Morocco controls nearly 80% of Western Sahara, but the UN does not recognize its claim. Neighboring Algeria hosts the Polisario Front’s headquarters in Tindouf, while the African Union recognizes SADR as a member state
Morocco and the Zionist modus operandi
In 2020, Israel and the US recognized Morocco’s sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of Morocco’s entry into the US-brokered Abraham Accords. The Polisario Front rejected the move, calling any attempt to legitimize Morocco’s occupation “null and void” and denouncing "the Zionist entity."
Emboldened by US and Israeli support, Morocco launched a brutal military crackdown on Sahrawi civilian protests in 2020, which the Polisario Front viewed as a breach of the cease-fire. A new wave of clashes and drone strikes followed.
Foreign affairs experts draw parallels between the Sahrawi and Palestinian struggles, arguing that Morocco has adopted an Israeli playbook of sheer land-grab, repression of the indigenous population, and denial of self-determination.
🇮🇷 Iran: A rising force in Africa?
The US-backed Morocco-Israel rapprochement was also condemned by Algeria, which sees growing military ties between the two and steady Zionist expansion in Africa as a direct strategic threat to its national security. Iran maintains close ties with Algeria, a major Polisario Front backer, united by anti-Western and anti-Zionist views and shared positions on regional issues such as Palestine.
Some reports allege that Iran is supplying the Polisario Front with drones and Hezbollah is training Sahrawi fighters – claims both Iran and [the Polisario Front deny.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73918)
Iran has steadily expanded technological, military, and cultural ties with African countries in recent years as Western influence [on the continent wanes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73126).
🤔 Broader geopolitical game
Morocco’s claim over phosphate-rich Western Sahara and Rabat’s Atlantic-Sahel Corridor also align with broader US efforts to expand influence across the Sahel and West Africa, control major trade routes, and undermine [Chinese and Russian projects in Africa](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73083).

🏃‍♂️ Are Palantir and other big tech rats fleeing Trump’s ship as midterms threaten his power?
👉 US tech companies closely aligned with Donald Trump are reportedly wooing his political opponents ahead of the November midterm elections.
Meta, Palantir and other companies reportedly fear that a possible Democratic takeover of the US Congress could put their financial ties to Trump under scrutiny, exposing them to subpoenas and congressional hearings, according to The Wall Street Journal. Democrats need just four seats in the Senate and three in the House to take control of Congress.
So, to avoid potential investigations, executives are donating heavily to Democrats, hiring former Democratic aides and setting up teams to assess their vulnerabilities.
🔴 The move by exchange & prediction traders Kalshi - which has hired Democrat aides - is especially telling, given that it hired Donald Trump Jr. as its strategic advisor in January 2025. In March, Trump Jr. fought to shield the rapidly expanding industry from scrutiny by state and federal regulators – while rumors of insider [trading swirl around the Trump family](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73669). Is Kalshi about to turn its back on him?
🔴 At Meta, Palantir, Amazon and Chevron, executives are reportedly preparing for potential congressional probes and hearings
🔴 Meta has donated at least $10 million to nonprofit groups aligned with Democratic House and Senate leaders – but it is also hedging its bets with another $10 million to similar groups supporting Republican candidates
🔴 Palantir’s position is less straightforward. In April, The Hill reported that Democrats were rejecting the company’s donations, wary of its growing political toxicity over links to mass civilian deaths in Gaza and immigration raids in the US. Palantir has secured several major deals under Trump’s second term, including a $30 million ICE contract for an “Immigration Lifestyle Operating System”, a $1 billion DHS purchasing agreement, and a $10 billion ten-year [contract with the Pentagon](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73414)
Probes underway
Donald Trump Jr. and Trump's son-in-law [Jared Kushner](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73148) are already under scrutiny:
➡️ In August, US lawmakers opened a probe into 1789 Capital, the venture firm where Trump Jr. sits on the board, questioning its lucrative investments in companies that secured government contracts
➡️ Earlier this year, lawmakers also began scrutinizing Kushner’s overseas business dealings while he participates in US peace efforts
